prompt_payload.task: Generate a small portfolio of executable cross-domain optimization skills. A skill may reshape the GP kernel and may add a source-neighbor prior only when leave-one-out target calibration supports it.

target_schema.boundary: Only public feature schema is exposed. No target outcomes are included.

transfer_card.evidence_summary: Compiled 4 active role transfers from real_suzuki_miyaura using 96 observed source rows and 0 conservative shared-vocabulary value priors. Direction is not transferred as a raw chemical rule; the card transfers role-level evidence strength and only transfers source value priors when source and target fields share the same public descriptor vocabulary.

base_policy.name: mixed_kernel_gp_ucb
base_policy.normalization: categorical weights are normalized to mean 1
base_policy.ensemble: multiple scales are aggregated by mean normalized candidate rank
base_policy.source_prior: mapped-role nearest-neighbor prediction from source observations; sign and strength are recalibrated using only currently revealed target observations

design_rules: Return diverse executable patches, not candidate IDs and not review prose.
At least one patch should include scale 0 as a target-only safety anchor in an ensemble.
At least one patch should focus on the two highest-confidence roles.
Include an exploration-first patch with gp_beta above 2.2 and gp_beta_end at or below 1.2.
Include a conservative patch with gp_beta and gp_beta_end both at or below 1.5.
Make at least one patch test a counter-hypothesis rather than only reinforcing the strongest source role.
Include at least two source-prior patches when mapped roles have shared vocabularies.
Use signed calibration when source and target objectives can be inversely related.
Use positive_only calibration only when the objective semantics support the same direction.
Set source_prior_strength to 0 when role vocabularies are not meaningfully comparable.
Downweight weak or semantically uncertain role mappings instead of treating all roles equally.
Use multi-scale ensembles when transfer strength is uncertain.
Do not claim access to target outcomes. Calibration and held-out evaluation happen after generation.

allowed_space.role_multipliers: map every target decision field to [0.20, 3.0]
allowed_space.gp_beta: number in [0.5, 3.0] used at the first replay round
allowed_space.gp_beta_end: number in [0.5, 3.0] reached linearly at the final replay round

patches.confidence: evidence-calibrated number in [0, 1]; do not reuse one default
patches.reason: brief hypothesis, counter-hypothesis, mechanism, and failure trigger

patches.reason: Hypothesis: ligand and aryl-halide role evidence improves the kernel; the scale-0 member protects against negative transfer. Rank averaging limits scale brittleness; fail if transferred scales consistently rank revealed outcomes worse than the anchor.

Hypothesis: the two highest-confidence mappings, ligand and aryl_halide, carry most transferable structure; weak additive and base mappings are suppressed. Failure trigger: revealed-target validation favors balanced or target-only geometry.

Hypothesis: broad early GP-UCB exploration can discover whether source-weighted categorical neighborhoods transfer before cooling toward exploitation. The target-only member and five scales hedge misspecification; fail if high-scale members remain poorly calibrated after reveals.

Hypothesis: modest ligand emphasis captures the strongest source evidence without overexploration or aggressive transfer. The counterweight is a scale-0 anchor; fail if leave-one-out target replay shows no gain over target-only ranking.

Counter-hypothesis: substrate identity may dominate Buchwald-Hartwig behavior even though ligand has higher source confidence. Strong aryl-halide weighting tests that mechanism; fail if revealed-target validation instead supports ligand-led or uniform similarity.

Counter-hypothesis: the reagent-to-base role mapping is more useful in the target chemistry than its confidence suggests. A target-only anchor and strict gain trigger contain the risk; fail if base-emphasized scales underperform during revealed-target replay.

Hypothesis: smoothly discounted role weights are safer than concentrating all similarity on one field. A broad scale ensemble averages uncertain transfer strength; fail if target replay selects either uniform geometry or a single-role extreme.

Counter-hypothesis: target-specific additive and base structure may matter despite weak source mappings. High temperature, a target-only anchor, and a stringent gain threshold make this a controlled stress test; fail on absent cross-validated improvement.
